channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Zhandos Shaimardanov Appointed New Director of Kazakhstan Institute for Strategic Studies
item.description: Zhandos Shaimardanov has been appointed the new director of the Kazakhstan Institute for Strategic Studies (KISI), replacing Yerkin Tukumo. Tukumo has been appointed Special Representative of the President for Afghanistan. KISI is a research institute under the President of Kazakhstan.

item.title: Mukhtar Tileuberdi Reappointed as Kazakhstan's Minister of Foreign Affairs
item.description: Mukhtar Tileuberdi has once again become the Minister of Foreign Affairs, succeeding Yermek Kosherbayev. Tileuberdi previously held the position from 2019 to 2023 before serving as ambassador to Austria.

item.title: Kazakh President Appoints New Ambassadors to Austria and Pakistan
item.description: Kazakhstan's President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has appointed new ambassadors to Austria and Pakistan. Yermek Kosherbayev will serve as Ambassador to Austria and Permanent Representative to international organizations in Vienna. Yerkin Tukumov has been appointed Ambassador to Pakistan. Saulekul Sailaukyzy was relieved of her ambassadorial duties in Morocco and Togo.

item.title: Scholarly Heritage of Transoxiana Presented at UNESCO Headquarters
item.description: An international conference on the scholarly heritage of Transoxiana was held at UNESCO headquarters in Paris, attended by over 300 scholars and diplomats. Participants discussed the contributions of Central Asian scholars to global civilization and the preservation of cultural heritage. The event was organized by the Center of Islamic Civilization in Uzbekistan and other partners.

item.title: Turkmenistan and EU Define Education Partnership Priorities Until 2034
item.description: Turkmenistan and the European Training Foundation (ETF) held a roundtable to define priorities for their education partnership until 2034. Discussions focused on modernizing vocational and higher education, digitalization, and developing skills in transport, logistics, energy, and digital communications. Joint action plans for 2028-2034 were outlined.

item.title: Kazakhstan Introduces 14-Day Cooling-Off Period for Unsecured Loans
item.description: Starting October 12, Kazakhstan citizens can withdraw from unsecured loans within 14 days without penalty. The Agency for Regulation and Development of the Financial Market introduced this rule. Borrowers must still pay interest for days the money was used. If additional insurance was purchased, it can also be cancelled, with unused premiums refunded minus bank's actual costs.

item.title: Kazakhstan Updates Driving Test Rules, Easing Procedures for Applicants
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Internal Affairs has implemented new rules for vehicle registration and driving tests, effective October 9. Procedures are simplified, eliminating separate inspections for vehicle modifications. Applicants can retake failed exams the next working day. After three unsuccessful attempts, subsequent retakes are paid. Positive theoretical exam results will no longer be invalidated if the practical exam is not passed.

item.title: Individuals Arrested in Tashkent Region for Involving Minors in Drug Trafficking
item.description: Authorities in the Tashkent region have arrested individuals for recruiting underage girls into drug trafficking operations. During special operations in Chirchiq city and Qibray district, a total of 4.7 kg of narcotics were seized. Among those apprehended were university students. Further details are available via the provided link.

item.title: Taliban Authority Reports 679 Fatalities from Natural Disasters in Afghanistan Over Past Year
item.description: Afghanistan's National Disaster Management Authority reports 679 deaths and 1,634 injuries from natural disasters in the past year. The authority also stated that 4,470 homes were destroyed and 17,664 were partially damaged. The International Day for Disaster Risk Reduction is observed annually on October 13.

item.title: Afghan Foreign Minister Tells EU Envoy Global Community Failed to Support Farmers' Alternative Livelihoods
item.description: Amir Khan Muttaqi, Afghanistan's acting foreign minister, told the EU special envoy that the international community has not sufficiently supported Afghan farmers with alternative livelihoods to combat narcotics. The EU envoy acknowledged Afghanistan's security and counter-narcotics achievements and pledged increased cooperation.

item.title: EU Special Representative Meets with Taliban Foreign Minister in Kabul
item.description: Thomas Frellesen, the new EU special envoy for Afghanistan, met with Taliban Foreign Minister Amir Khan Muttaqi in Kabul to discuss security and counter-narcotics efforts. Muttaqi complained about the international community's failure to support alternative livelihoods for farmers. Frellesen pledged increased EU cooperation.

item.title: Uzbekistan Appoints First Deputy Prime Minister to Coordinate Education, Science, and Health Sectors
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev signed a decree to improve the executive structure of the Cabinet of Ministers, introducing a new position for the First Deputy Prime Minister overseeing education and science. Erkinjon Turdimov, formerly governor of Sirdaryo region, has been appointed to this role. He will coordinate ministries and regional authorities in education, science, and healthcare.

item.title: Kazakhstan Sees Decrease in Apartment Sales and Purchases in September
item.description: In September 2026, Kazakhstan registered 35,406 housing sale and purchase transactions, a 1.1% decrease compared to August. Almaty and Astana led in transaction volume, accounting for 20.5% and 17.3% respectively. The Ulytau region recorded the fewest transactions. While some regions saw growth, others, including Almaty, experienced a decline.

item.title: Tajikistan and Switzerland Discuss New Joint Projects to Boost Economic Cooperation
item.description: Tajikistan's Minister of Economic Development and Trade met with the Head of the Swiss Cooperation Office to discuss enhancing trade and economic relations. Key areas of focus included simplifying trade procedures, attracting investment, and developing tourism infrastructure. Both sides expressed readiness to implement new joint projects.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Introduce Fees for Repeated Driving Test Attempts
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Internal Affairs is amending regulations for vehicle registration and driver's license exams. Candidates failing the theoretical or practical exam three times will face fees for subsequent attempts. The changes aim to ensure applicants possess strong knowledge before taking the tests. Foreign license exchanges will also require passing a theoretical exam and verification of the original document.

item.title: Philippines to Open Embassy in Astana, Kazakhstan
item.description: Kazakhstan and the Philippines discussed bilateral cooperation priorities during a meeting between Kazakhstan's Foreign Minister Mukhtar Tileuberdi and Philippine Deputy Foreign Minister Leo M. Herrera-Lim. Kazakhstan welcomed the Philippines' intention to open an embassy in Astana, believing it will deepen bilateral ties and expand practical interaction. Both sides expressed interest in maintaining regular political dialogue.

item.title: Kazakhstan Reports Five Cases of Swine Flu, Ministry Issues Health Advice
item.description: Kazakhstan has registered five laboratory-confirmed cases of influenza A(H1N1)pdm09, commonly known as swine flu, in Astana and Mangystau region. The Ministry of Health stated that the epidemiological situation is under control. Symptoms include sudden high fever, headache, chills, muscle aches, cough, and sore throat. The main risk is developing viral pneumonia.

item.title: KamAZ Truck Collides with Two Motorcycles in Kostanay, One Fatality Reported
item.description: A KamAZ truck collided with two motorcycles in Tobyl city, Kostanay region, resulting in the death of one motorcyclist at the scene. According to the Kostanay Regional Police Department, the truck driver failed to ensure safety while turning left and entered the main road. The second motorcyclist was hospitalized with injuries.

item.title: Central Asian Nations Warn Citizens of Dangers Following Saudi Arabia Attacks
item.description: Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, and Uzbekistan have issued warnings to their citizens in Saudi Arabia following attacks on civilian infrastructure. They advise increased caution, following local authorities' guidance, avoiding non-essential travel to airports, checking flight statuses, and staying away from crowded places. Citizens are urged to postpone non-urgent trips and contact embassies in emergencies.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Housing Market Sees Decline in Sales, Almaty and Astana Lead Transactions
item.description: In September 2026, Kazakhstan registered 35,406 housing sale and purchase transactions, a 1.1% decrease from the previous month. Apartment sales dropped by 2.2%, while individual house transactions increased by 2.7%. Almaty, Astana, and Karaganda region saw the most activity, though some regions experienced significant declines. Year-on-year, sales fell by 14.3%.

item.title: Kazakhstan Introduces Paid Retakes for Driving Test After Three Failed Attempts
item.description: Kazakhstan plans to amend rules for obtaining driver's licenses, making retakes of the driving test paid after three unsuccessful attempts. According to the Ministry of Internal Affairs, these changes aim to simplify procedures. Successful theoretical exam results will no longer be invalidated if the practical part is failed.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan President Orders Expedited Citizenship for Ethnic Kyrgyz; Uzbek Woman Granted Relief
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's President Sadyr Japarov has ordered that ethnic Kyrgyz be granted citizenship within one day. This directive followed an appeal from an Uzbek woman married to a Kyrgyz citizen, who faced difficulties obtaining citizenship. Japarov instructed officials to resolve her issue promptly.

item.title: Kazakhstan Woman Awarded Compensation After Food Poisoning at Wedding
item.description: A woman in Kazakhstan has successfully sued a restaurant owner for food poisoning contracted at a wedding. She was awarded 220,000 tenge for medical expenses and moral damages after 188 people fell ill. Criminal proceedings were initiated following the mass poisoning incident.

item.title: Iran Finalizing Response to US Views on Nuclear Deal Proposal
item.description: Iran's deputy foreign minister stated that Tehran is finalizing its response to US concerns regarding a proposal submitted in New York. Iran welcomes diplomacy and negotiations, and will communicate its final position through mediators after consultations. The official also accused the US of violating commitments.

item.title: Afghanistan's Hairatan Port Facilitates Over 280 Daily Freight Wagon Arrivals from Central Asia
item.description: The Hairatan railway port in northern Afghanistan receives between 280 and 300 freight wagons daily from Central Asian countries. This highlights its growing role in connecting Afghanistan to regional and international markets, including China. The railway transports goods like clothing, machinery, and electrical equipment.

item.title: Global Oil Prices Decline After Recent Surge, WTI and Brent See Drops
item.description: Global oil prices fell on Tuesday, reversing recent gains. WTI crude futures dropped 1.63% to $92.21 per barrel, while Brent crude fell 1.52% to $105.03. Russian Urals crude saw a significant 8.47% decrease to $118.23. The decline follows a previous rise attributed to supply disruption fears.

item.title: Gorno-Badakhshan Autonomous Region in Tajikistan Commissions 1800 Facilities Over Five Years
item.description: Over the past five years, 1800 facilities have been commissioned in the Gorno-Badakhshan Autonomous Region (GBAO) of Tajikistan. The regional head highlighted the role of local labor and entrepreneurs in developing infrastructure, including social and economic projects. Efforts continue in agriculture, education, and youth development.

item.title: Azerbaijan: School hijab ban sparks widespread protests and boycotts
item.description: New regulations in Azerbaijan prohibiting hijabs in state schools have led to mass protests. Hundreds gathered in Baku and other regions, with students boycotting classes. The ban, introduced on September 21, prohibits additional clothing elements that violate uniform requirements and secular education principles. Some schools reportedly denied entry to students and teachers wearing hijabs, prompting demonstrations.

item.title: Philippines plans to open embassy in Kazakhstan's capital, Astana
item.description: The Philippines intends to establish an embassy in Astana, Kazakhstan. This was discussed during a meeting between Kazakhstan's Foreign Minister Mukhtar Tileuberdi and Philippine Deputy Foreign Minister Leo M. Herrera-Lim. Both sides explored prospects for bilateral relations, trade, economic, and investment cooperation, as well as collaboration within the UN and ASEAN. The establishment of a permanent diplomatic mission is expected to strengthen ties.

item.title: 99 foreign nationals expelled from Kazakhstan for migration law violations
item.description: In the Pavlodar region of Kazakhstan, 99 foreign nationals have been expelled from the country for violating migration laws. Over the past nine months, 6,279 individuals faced administrative penalties for such violations, including 1,504 foreigners. Additionally, 119 employers were held accountable for breaking rules on hiring foreign labor. The police reported that 595 foreigners obtained Kazakh citizenship during this period.

item.title: Iran's IRGC Commander Warns External Powers Against Hormuz Strait Intervention
item.description: Ahmad Vahidi, commander of Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC), has warned external powers against intervening in the Strait of Hormuz and the Persian Gulf. He stated that no power outside the region has the right to maintain a dominant presence there. This warning comes amid a significant US military presence in the Persian Gulf and the Strait of Hormuz, and Iran's continued claims of full control over the waterway.

item.title: Astana Faces No Water Shortages After Infrastructure Upgrades
item.description: Astana experienced water shortages in previous years due to delayed infrastructure projects. The commissioning of a new pumping and filtering station has stabilized the situation. State media reported that officials responsible for developing the city's engineering infrastructure failed to perform their duties diligently, leading to the crisis. The city is currently fully dependent on the Astana water reservoir, which poses a significant risk.

item.title: Kazakhmys Intensifies Geological Exploration to Develop Zhezkazgan Deposits
item.description: Kazakhmys Corporation is intensifying geological exploration at the Zhezkazgan deposit to identify additional copper reserves and expand the raw material base for existing mines. Special attention is given to areas under contract №114, crucial for the further development of Zhezkazgan's mining enterprises. The company views developing the mineral resource base as a priority long-term objective.

item.title: Kazakhstan Issues Warning to inDrive After Price Surge Amid Yandex Data Center Attacks
item.description: Kazakhstan's Agency for Protection and Development of Competition issued a warning to inDrive following reports of sharp price increases on October 11, coinciding with disruptions to Yandex Go. The agency noted increased demand for inDrive as users switched from Yandex. Prices reportedly tripled in some instances. The warning aims to prevent potential antitrust violations.

item.title: Uzbekistan Military Team Secures Silver Medal at UK's Cambrian Patrol Competition
item.description: A team of military personnel from Uzbekistan's Ministry of Defense won a silver medal at the international Cambrian Patrol competition held in Wales, UK. Over 140 patrol groups from approximately 35 countries participated. Participants navigated challenging terrains for 48 hours, demonstrating skills in reconnaissance, combat scenarios, obstacle crossing, and first aid.

item.title: Over 6,000 Affected by Earthquake in Panama, No Fatalities Reported
item.description: More than 6,000 people have been affected by an earthquake in Panama, with no reported fatalities. President Laurentino Cortizo stated that 1,744 homes have been inspected and the number of affected individuals may be updated as inspections continue. The government is providing food, water, and restoring infrastructure, including electricity and roads.

item.title: UN Secretary-General Highlights Global Child Marriage Crisis on International Day of the Girl Child
item.description: UN Secretary-General António Guterres stated that a child marriage occurs every three seconds globally, depriving girls of their childhood. One in five girls worldwide marries before 18. Poverty, conflict, climate shocks, and displacement exacerbate the issue. Guterres urged measures like education, economic empowerment, and legal protection to end the practice.

item.title: Bronze Age Structures, Hearth, and Child's Grave Discovered at Jarqo'ton Archaeological Site
item.description: Archaeological excavations at the Jarqo'ton site in Surxondaryo region have uncovered Bronze Age structures, a hearth, and a child's grave. The findings, dating back to the 3rd-1st millennium BC, include intact pottery and offer insights into the lifestyle and burial customs of the ancient population.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Detains Critic Syrak Kenzhebaev Abroad, Brings Him to Bishkek
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Interior Ministry announced the detention of Syrak Kenzhebaev abroad and his subsequent transfer to Bishkek, where he was placed in a temporary detention facility. The ministry alleges he incited mass unrest and defrauded an individual of $150,000. Kenzhebaev had previously been detained in 2019 and released during 2020 protests.

item.title: Pakistan Rejects Taliban Spokesperson's Remarks, Demands Action Against TTP
item.description: Pakistan's Ministry of Information and Broadcasting rejected comments by Taliban spokesman Zabihullah Mujahid, stating that Afghan authorities should address the presence of the Pakistani Taliban (TTP) in Afghanistan. Pakistan cited a UN report estimating 6,000 TTP fighters in Afghanistan and urged concrete action from the Taliban, criticizing their human rights record.
